Concern.description:
A user-specific, ongoing focus of attention that can be associated with resources, concepts, and entities to provide personal context and organizational structure.
A Concern does not represent identity (that's Self), work execution (that's Work), or knowledge structure (that's Information); instead, it binds other entities together under a shared focus.
Concerns operate as an OVERLAY LAYER, independent of deeper domains. A user may be concerned about something without it being part of their identity or formal work.

ProjectConcern.description:
A Concern representing a concrete project with defined scope, resources, timeline, and expected outcome. A project is something you work on, with a beginning and an end.
Distinct from Work::Project (execution structure) or Self::Goal (enduring aspiration). A ProjectConcern is a personal focus area that may or may not be formalized as work.

GoalConcern.description:
A Concern representing a goal, target state, or objective that the user is working toward. A goal describes where you want to be, with a measurable or observable target condition.
Distinct from Self::Goal (enduring aspiration). A GoalConcern is a time-limited focus ("run a 5K in under 25 minutes this month"); a Self::Goal is a long-term aspiration ("become a healthier person over my lifetime").

AreaConcern.description:
A Concern representing a broad area of life that the user is paying attention to. An area is a long-term, ongoing category of focus (e.g., Health, Career, Family, Finance).
AreaConcerns are typically stable and can be hierarchical (Health → Fitness → Running). Distinct from Self::Role (identity-based) or Principle (value-based). An AreaConcern is "what I'm paying attention to in this domain right now".

RoutineConcern.description:
A Concern representing a recurring practice, habit, or regular commitment that the user maintains. A routine is something you do regularly (daily, weekly, etc.) to support your life or work.
Captures the idea of an ongoing practice that is part of your current focus without being a project or a goal. Distinct from Self::Habit (stable behavioral pattern) or Work::Task (one-off execution). A RoutineConcern is "what I'm practicing right now".

LogConcern.description:
A Concern representing an ongoing log, journal, or time-series tracking mechanism that the user maintains. A log is a structured record of data or observations over time, often supporting routine practices or goal tracking.
Distinct from individual log entries (those are Resources) or the practice of logging (that's RoutineConcern). A LogConcern is the ongoing system itself.

LearningConcern.description:
A Concern representing a learning track, course, or skill development journey that the user is pursuing. A learning concern is a structured path toward acquiring knowledge or capability in a domain.
Distinct from a GoalConcern (though learning may support a goal) or Self::Capability (the outcome). A LearningConcern is the learning journey itself.

TopicTaxonomy.description: A named grouping scheme that contains a set of related topics. It is analogous to a SKOS ConceptScheme. A taxonomy serves as the container within which all topics are organized and classified. Every Topic must belong to exactly one TopicTaxonomy.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier

slug.description: URL-safe identifier for the topic. Follows kebab-case naming convention (lowercase alphanumerics with hyphens as separators).

aliases.description: Alternative names or labels for the topic. SKOS altLabels providing equivalent terms that users might search for or use to refer to this topic.

materialized_path.description: Pre-computed ancestor path showing the hierarchical position of this topic. Format: /parent/child/grandchild. Enables efficient hierarchy queries without traversal.

created_on.description: When this relationship was created or asserted.

has_parent_topics.description: Set of parent topics in the polyhierarchical structure. A topic can have zero or more parents, enabling multiple classification perspectives. No cycles allowed (DAG constraint).

has_child_topics.description: Set of child topics in the polyhierarchical structure. Topics can have zero or more children depending on their position in the hierarchy.

Topic.description: A focused concept or subject within a TopicTaxonomy. It represents a discrete idea, category, or area of focus that can be used to classify and tag resources, activities, and other entities. Topics form a polyhierarchical graph (multiple parents allowed) within their parent taxonomy.

confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) expressing degree of certainty in the annotation

evidence.description: Notes on the basis of the match. Optional field providing rationale, methodology, or supporting information for how this alignment was established.

Match.description: A first-class entity recording the alignment of a local Topic or TopicTaxonomy to a concept in an external ontology system. It carries confidence score, provenance information, and evidence notes. Enables rich semantic alignment with external systems like Wikidata, CSO, LCSH, MeSH, UNSPSC, Schema.org, DBpedia, etc.

has_principles.description: Links an Organism to the principles (rules) derived from their alignment that govern behavior and decisions.

has_behaviors.description: Links an Organism to their behaviors (Methods, Processes, Routines, Habits) that manifest alignment with their principles.

has_vision.description: Links an Organism to their long-term aspirational visions about who they want to become or what they want to create.

has_goals.description: Links an Organism to their time-bound, measurable goals that work toward their visions.

PhysicalObject.description: A subtype of Object representing things that have material, spatial, and temporal existence. Physical objects occupy space, have mass or substance, and persist or decay in the physical world. Examples: laptop, car, house, tool, furniture, book (physical artifact).

DigitalObject.description: A subtype of Object representing things that exist as information or computation artifacts. Digital objects exist as data, code, or computational states within digital systems and do not have physical substance except as electronic memory. Examples: file, application, web service, API, library, database, account, cloud service.

Asset.description: A representation of an Object (physical or digital) that the organism actively uses, depends on, manages, or owns. An Asset tracks the organism's relationship to an Object: how it is used, how long it has been in use, and its value or criticality. Semantically a "possessive use relationship" reified as an entity, enabling lifecycle tracking and dependency modeling. Inherits from Object for schema simplicity while representing a relationship layer between organism and world.

Person.description: An individual human being in the external World domain, distinct from Organism (Self domain) who is the central subject of the ontology. A Person has identity, agency, and the capacity to interact with the organism, participate in work, and form relationships. Promoted to carry_forward status in Phase 3 World domain boundary work.

context_or_meaning.description: Context in which the relationship originated or operates

Relationship.description: A first-class entity modeling a bond, interaction pattern, or ongoing connection between the organism and one or more Persons, or between Persons. A Relationship captures the quality, type, history, and nature of interpersonal bonds. Enables sophisticated social modeling, community detection, and collaboration planning. Promoted to carry_forward status in Phase 3 World domain boundary work.

title.description: Name of the community (e.g., "My Team," "Hiking Club," "Family")

Community.description: An organized or coherent group of Persons who share identity, purpose, or ongoing interaction. A Community is a higher-order social structure composed of Persons and the Relationships between them. Enables modeling of teams, families, communities of practice, hobby groups, organizations, and any organized group. Promoted to carry_forward status in Phase 3 World domain boundary work.

themes.description: Knowledge organization systems (KOS) used to classify resources in this catalog. Typically SKOS ConceptSchemes or similar.

has_resources.description: Member resources in this collection or catalog. For Collection, typically untyped. For Catalog, typically via typed CatalogEntry mechanism.

Catalog.description: Resource representing curated, governed collection of related Resources using DCAT semantics. Enables typed relationships, formal curation, semantic clarity, and interoperability.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier

repository_type.description: System classification (local, cloud, hybrid, distributed, version_control)

created_on.description: When this relationship was created or asserted.

web_url.description: Public web interface URL if available (e.g., web UI for cloud service)

Repository.description: First-class entity representing a system or application storing and managing resources. Examples: Obsidian vault, Safari bookmarks, Zotero, Raindrop, GitHub, file system, Heptabase, Readwise. Captures provenance, system-specific metadata, and cross-system queries.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier for this entity

uri.description: Explicit RDF IRI if different from id

target.description: The target being annotated (Resource, Entity, or Concept URI/CURIE)

Annotation.description: A provisional or confirmed assertion made by an automated system or human about a resource, entity, or concept. Carries target, value, confidence score, and explicit lifecycle state, enabling incremental knowledge enrichment with provenance tracking. Serves as optional first-class extension layer above core ontology.

QualifiedLink.description: Abstract base class for first-class relationships carrying semantic metadata in addition to source and target. Specialized qualified link classes (ResourceTopicLink, EffortActivityLink, etc.) extend this pattern across the ontology.

resource_concern_role.description: Semantic role of the resource in the concern. Values: canonical_logbook (primary record), supporting_log (secondary record), reference (background material), evidence (supports claims), summary (progress), inspiration (guides direction), plan (execution plan), todo_list (task list), other

link_confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) that the resource-concern association is correct. 0.5 = uncertain; 1.0 = highly confident.

link_created_by.description: Who created this link (user, system, ML model). Format: "user:alice", "system:import", "llm:claude"

ResourceConcernLink.description:
A first-class association linking a Resource (from Knowledge Management domain) to a Concern, capturing the role the resource plays in that concern and metadata about the association (confidence, provenance, creation timestamp).
Implements the "qualified link" pattern: relationships are not merely edges but entities with their own properties. Enables rich provenance-aware associations.
Example: A "Meals Log" document linked to a health area concern with role="canonical_logbook" and confidence=0.95.

concern_concept_role.description: Semantic role of the concept in the concern. Values: primary_theme (main topic), secondary_theme (supporting topic), metric (what is measured), constraint (what limits it), risk_factor (what risk), background_context (contextual knowledge), other

link_confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) that the concept-concern association is correct.

link_created_by.description: Who created this link (user, system, ML model).

ConcernConceptLink.description:
A first-class association linking a Concept/Topic (from Information domain) to a Concern, capturing the role the concept plays in that concern and metadata about the association.
Enables concerns to express what they are about (themes), what they measure (metrics), what constrains them (constraints), and what risks they face (risk factors).
Example: A health area concern linked to "Nutrition" concept with role="primary_theme" and confidence=0.9.

concern_entity_role.description: Semantic role of the entity in the concern (NOT RBAC). Values: owner (responsible), target_person (benefits/affected), collaborator (works with), coach (provides coaching), mentor (provides mentoring), stakeholder (affected by outcome), dependent (depends on outcome), other

link_confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) that the entity-concern association is correct.

link_created_by.description: Who created this link (user, system, ML model).

ConcernEntityLink.description:
A first-class polymorphic association linking an Entity (from World/Self domain) to a Concern, capturing the role that entity plays in that concern and metadata about the association.
Enables concerns to express who is involved: owners (responsible), collaborators (work together), coaches/mentors (guidance), stakeholders (affected), targets (benefit).
IMPORTANT: Roles are semantic descriptors of participation, NOT RBAC (access control). Access control belongs in application layer. (T-5 decision, Phase 3)
Example: A project concern with entity="john_smith" role="owner" and confidence=1.0.

edge_role.description: Semantic relationship type between parent and child topics. Indicates the nature of the connection (broader/narrower/part_of/instance_of/related).

TopicEdge.description: A directed relationship between two topics, representing a specific semantic connection type (e.g., "broader", "narrower", "part_of", "instance_of", "related"). Edges form the semantic backbone of the topic hierarchy.

depth.description: Number of edges in the path from ancestor to descendant. 0 indicates self-relation (ancestor equals descendant); 1 indicates direct parent-child relationship; n indicates transitive relation through n edges.

TopicClosure.description: A pre-computed transitive closure of the topic hierarchy. It records all ancestor-descendant pairs and the depth (distance) between them. This enables efficient queries like "find all ancestors of topic X". A performance optimization that has ontological significance by making explicit which topics are transitively related.

relationship_type.description: Type of relationship (organizes, supports, incubates, explores_for)

role.description: Role of activity in effort (primary, supporting, context)

creator.description: User or system that created the link

EffortActivityLink.description: Qualified link from an Effort to an Activity, indicating organizational, strategic, or causal relationship. Carries role, confidence, and provenance metadata. Enables many-to-many relationship between Efforts and Activities.

role.description: Role of effort in goal implementation (primary, supporting, exploratory)

creator.description: User or system that created the link

GoalEffortLink.description: Qualified link from a Goal (Self domain) to an Effort, indicating that the Effort implements or advances the Goal. Forward reference; Goal class defined in Self domain.

creator.description: User or system that created the link

ActivityTopicLink.description: Qualified link from an Activity to a Topic (Information domain), indicating that the work is about, informed by, or aligned with the topic. Forward reference; Topic class defined in Information domain.

creator.description: User or system that created the link

EffortTopicLink.description: Qualified link from an Effort to a Topic (Information domain), indicating that strategic work is aligned with or organized around topical domains. Forward reference; Topic class defined in Information domain.

role.description: Role of resource (primary_source, supporting_reference, evidence, requirement, background)

creator.description: User or system that created the link

ActivityResourceLink.description: Qualified link from an Activity to a Resource (Knowledge Management domain), indicating that the work uses, produces, or references the resource. Forward reference; Resource class defined in KM domain.

role.description: Role of resource (primary_input, supporting_resource, output, evidence)

creator.description: User or system that created the link

EffortResourceLink.description: Qualified link from an Effort to a Resource (Knowledge Management domain), indicating that strategic work spans resources as inputs or outputs. Forward reference; Resource class defined in KM domain.

role.description: Semantic role in a qualified relationship. Examples: primary_subject, keyword_mention, background, evidence, reference, uses, produces.

confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) expressing degree of certainty in the annotation

provenance.description: Provenance or explanation of how the relationship was determined (system-determined, human-curated, ml-classified, etc.)

ResourceTopicLink.description: Qualified link from a Resource to a Topic carrying role, confidence, and provenance metadata. Formally expresses resource subject classification with semantic richness beyond simple tagging.

role.description: uses, produces, references, evidence, requirement, background

confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0–1.0) expressing degree of certainty in the annotation

provenance.description: Provenance or explanation of how the relationship was determined (system-determined, human-curated, ml-classified, etc.)

ResourceActivityLink.description: Qualified link from a Resource to an Activity carrying role, confidence, and provenance. Formalizes work support relationships (uses, produces, references) with semantic metadata.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier for this entity

title.description: Human-readable display name (required per domain via slot_usage)

Entity.description: The logical root abstraction for all things that have identity in the ontology. An Entity is anything that can be named, tracked through time, and related to other things. All domain classes inherit from Entity. Not directly instantiated.

title.description: Name or label for the problem

description.description: What is the problem and why it matters?

severity.description: Impact severity scale (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)

impact_areas.description: What domains or entities are affected

resolution_status.description: Current state (IDENTIFIED, ANALYZED, ADDRESSING, RESOLVED, ACCEPTED)

Problem.description: A factual difficulty or undesired state that needs to be addressed or resolved, requiring attention from Work (Task) or Self (Behavior) domains. Problems are present or chronic adversities that affect Self.Organism, Work Projects, or World Assets. Problems form the umbrella for Struggle, Worry, and Emergency subtypes.

title.description: Name or label for the condition

condition_type.description: Category (HEALTH, ENVIRONMENTAL, SYSTEM, SOCIAL, FINANCIAL, OTHER)

affecting_entity.description: What entity does this condition affect

Condition.description: An intrinsic, ongoing state or circumstance affecting an entity (Organism, Asset, Location) that is neither inherently bad nor good but constrains or enables action. Conditions are distinct from Problems in that they are states, not difficulties. Forms the umbrella for HealthCondition, EnvironmentalCondition, and SystemCondition subtypes.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier

Identity.description: The constellation of roles, archetypes, and areas of importance that define "who I am" or "who I aspire to be." Conceptual grouping treating multifaceted nature of personhood. Currently no formal class; Roles and Archetypes link directly to Organism.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier

enacts_principle.description: Links a Behavior to the Principle(s) it concretely enacts or manifests. Direct relationship, not first-class qualified link (per C-SELF-4).

implements_goal.description: Links a Behavior to the Goal(s) it works toward. Direct relationship, not first-class qualified link (per C-SELF-4).

Behavior.description: Any physical manifestation, action, or pattern that you enact to live in alignment with your principles — ranging from deliberate techniques to deeply habituated automatic responses. Treated as spectrum from conscious to automatic, though categories are not mutually exclusive.

id.description: Canonical logical identifier

Delta.description: Any specific, individual change or transformation that is desired — representing a gap between current state and desired state in a particular dimension. Parent class for Outcome and Action.

title.description: Name or label for the object

description.description: What the object is and its purpose

Object.description: An abstract representation of any thing that exists in the world with definable boundaries and persistent identity. Objects are the base class for anything physical or digital that the organism might interact with, own, use, or depend on.

Resource.description: Abstract base class for any information artifact that can be stored, retrieved, and organized. Logical ontology concept, distinct from storage implementation. Resources are fundamental to knowledge management and provide unified abstraction enabling cross-system querying.

LifeDomainEnum.description: Controlled vocabulary for annotating which high-level domain an entity belongs to. Used as a machine-readable organizational hint and navigation aid, not as a runtime type system. Multiple domains can apply to a single entity conceptually, but primary domain is indicated here.

ConcernTypeEnum.description: Runtime discriminator for concern types. Allows runtime polymorphism without creating explicit class hierarchy.

ConcernStatusEnum.description: Simple three-state lifecycle for concerns in the focus layer. Simpler than Effort (6 states) or Activity (5 states) because Concerns are about focus, not execution detail.

ConcernEntityRoleEnum.description: Semantic roles describing how an entity participates in a concern. IMPORTANT: These are semantic descriptors of involvement, NOT RBAC roles. Access control is an application-layer responsibility. (T-5 decision, Phase 3)

SeverityEnum.description: Severity scale for problems and conditions

TimeHorizonEnum.description: Time horizons for aspirational statements (Vision, etc.)

MonitoringFrequencyEnum.description: Frequency for risk monitoring and assessment

SystemTypeEnum.description: Category of system in a SystemCondition

ThreatLevelEnum.description: Inherent danger level of a hazard

ExposureFrequencyEnum.description: Frequency of exposure to a hazard

ReadinessLevelEnum.description: Proficiency or readiness level for a capability

EdgeRoleEnum.description: Enumeration of semantic relationship types between topics. Defines the specific nature of the directed relationship from parent to child.

MatchTypeEnum.description: Enumeration of alignment match types between local Topics and external ontologies. Directly aligned with SKOS matching vocabulary.

EntityTypeEnum.description: Enumeration of entity types that can be aligned to external systems in Match records.

EffortStatusEnum.description: States in the strategic commitment lifecycle

ActivityStatusEnum.description: States in the operational work lifecycle

ActivityTypeEnum.description: Runtime discriminator values for Activity types. This is a base enum of canonical types; applications may extend with custom types at runtime. The activity_type slot uses string range with designates_type: true for runtime flexibility.

RelationshipTypeEnum.description: Enumeration of relationship types between World entities. Working set of 9 core values; formal finalization deferred to Phase 2.

NoteTypeEnum.description: Classification of note types for Note.note_type discriminator

DocumentTypeEnum.description: Functional classification of documents for Document.document_type discriminator

AnnotationTypeEnum.description: Enumeration of assertion types annotations can make about their targets. topic_classification and entity_linking carry well-defined value types; summary, keyphrase, sentiment, and concern_linking value ranges deferred.

AnnotationStatusEnum.description: Three-state lifecycle for annotations. Transitions are explicit (no automatic progression). Rejected annotations are retained for audit trail; no reactivation of rejected status.
